{"task": {"id": "I_kwDOVRkquM8AAAABYs7_EQ", "item_id": "PVTI_lAHOAHSLSM4Bn_T5zhCR01o", "project_id": "PVT_kwHOAHSLSM4Bn_T5", "number": 3, "title": "Build a playable SNES emulator in Rust and WebAssembly using licensed homebrew games", "body": "## Problem

`snes-rust` currently contains development documentation only. We want to move directly to a **genuinely playable browser-based SNES emulator**, rather than stop at a workspace scaffold or a CPU-only proof of concept. The emulation core must be implemented **from scratch in Rust**, without importing or wrapping an existing SNES emulator or emulation core.

The long-term goal is compatibility with legally obtained commercial SNES cartridges. **This issue's concrete, verifiable first release** is a complete end-to-end, playable baseline using multiple independently developed, legally redistributable SNES homebrew games and hardware test ROMs. Passing a single static-screen demo is not enough.

## Expected outcome

A user can open the local browser app, select a licensed SNES `.sfc`/`.smc` image, and **start, control, hear, and play through real homebrew gameplay** at usable speed. The same Rust core supports automated native/headless regression tests and WebAssembly execution. The implementation forms a sound base for improving commercial-game compatibility; it does **not** claim full SNES catalog compatibility.

Keep this work under **one end-to-end delivery Issue**, with an internal checklist. Implement iteratively and open a focused PR (or a small, coherent PR series referencing this Issue) without considering the Issue complete until all required acceptance checks are met. Follow [the repository's development flow](../blob/main/docs/development-flow.md) and review guidance. Do not close it for a partial implementation.

## Scope / implementation tasks

- [ ] Initialize a minimal Rust workspace with a platform-independent `snes-core`, a `snes-wasm` adapter, a browser frontend, deterministic native/headless tests, and documented development/build commands. Choose only necessary dependencies; **no third-party emulation engine**.
- [ ] Implement ROM loading and cartridge metadata/mapping (at least ordinary LoROM, and HiROM if needed by the selected test set), header/copier-header handling, reset vectors, WRAM/SRAM, memory-mapped I/O and open-bus behavior required by target games.
- [ ] Implement the Ricoh 5A22 / 65C816 CPU (native/emulation modes, 8/16-bit register modes, addressing modes, instructions, flags, stack, interrupts, WAI/STP behavior and tested bus timing), with automated CPU regression coverage.
- [ ] Implement a master-clock/event-driven synchronization model for CPU, PPU, DMA/HDMA and audio; VBlank/HBlank, NMI/IRQ, timers, joypad serial reads and auto-read as exercised by targets. Avoid hard-coded per-game fixes.
- [ ] Implement the PPU register model and the graphics needed by the target games (VRAM/CGRAM/OAM, tiles, tilemaps, scrolling, BG modes, sprites, priority, windows, color math, Mode 7 where relevant, and mid-frame effects where used). Render actual emulated framebuffer pixels, not game-specific visual reproductions.
- [ ] Implement the APU/SPC700 boot and main-CPU communication, SPC700 execution, timers, S-DSP mixing/BRR/echo and audio buffering necessary for working **music and sound effects** in the required games.
- [ ] Expose the core via WebAssembly; build a static-site browser app with local ROM file picker, play/pause/reset, keyboard controls, gamepad support, framebuffer scaling, synchronized audio via Web Audio, user-gesture audio activation and clear error messages. ROMs should remain client-side.
- [ ] Implement/save battery-backed SRAM where supported, preserve it across browser sessions, and make load/reset semantics explicit.
- [ ] Add trace/logging/debug facilities and deterministic headless ROM runner, with automated assertions for CPU states, pass/fail markers, frame hashes/screenshots, input replay and bounded execution/timeouts. Provide actionable failure diagnostics.
- [ ] Add build, lint, unit/integration and browser end-to-end checks to CI, plus a clear README describing supported features, limitations, how to run the browser app, and how to run tests.

## Legal test games and verification assets

**Candidate playable homebrew games** (independent SNES programs; verify every code/art/audio/build artifact's distribution rights before importing or shipping a ROM):

1. [donth77/snes-homebrew — Gothicvania](https://github.com/donth77/snes-homebrew) — repository **MIT**, with CC0 attribution for third-party graphics; action-platformer with scrolling, HDMA, audio, controller input. Good high-feature end-to-end game target.
2. [undisbeliever/castle_platformer](https://github.com/undisbeliever/castle_platformer) — repository **MIT**, graphics attributed as **CC0**; a distinct playable platformer/engine exercising movement, tiles, sprites and dynamic scenes.
3. [BenjaminSchulte/SureInstinct](https://github.com/BenjaminSchulte/SureInstinct) — repository **MIT**; additional game candidate if its build and all included assets/ROM rights are confirmed. Do not make this difficult third-party build a substitute for the two required games.

**Hardware test ROMs**:

- [gilyon/snes-tests](https://github.com/gilyon/snes-tests) — **MIT**; 65C816 and SPC700 CPU ROM tests with expected results.
- [undisbeliever/snes-test-roms](https://github.com/undisbeliever/snes-test-roms) — **zlib**; PPU/timing/DMA/HDMA behavior checks.

For each checked-in or auto-fetched asset record its upstream URL, pinned commit/release, precise artifact, SHA-256, applicable license, copyright notices, asset/submodule/toolchain provenance and redistribution decision (e.g. `tests/roms/PROVENANCE.md`). Include required license/notice text. **A repository-level code license alone must not be treated as proof that every binary, third-party asset or prebuilt ROM is redistributable.** Build from audited source if appropriate; if permission is uncertain, keep that ROM user-supplied/ignored and select an alternative with clear rights. Never bundle copyrighted commercial ROMs, Nintendo firmware, or ROMs merely because they are free to download. Do not copy emulator implementation code from another project.

## Pre-merge acceptance

- [ ] The Rust CPU/core and both platform targets compile; documented local commands and all configured CI gates (format, lint, unit tests, integration tests and web production build) pass.
- [ ] A **minimum of two distinct playable homebrew game ROMs**, with the complete distribution/build-license audit recorded, boot through the **same generic emulation core** in the browser. Prefer Gothicvania and Castle Platformer; replace either with another similarly licensed *actual game* only if technically or legally blocked, documenting the reason.
- [ ] For **each** of those two games, an automated browser or recorded-input end-to-end test starts from reset, navigates beyond the title screen, exercises controller-driven gameplay (movement and at least one game interaction), verifies changing game-derived video frames, and runs for a documented substantial sample (e.g. >= 5 minutes of emulated gameplay) without panic, hang or uncontrolled desynchronization. Verify a reachable game-state transition/end screen where the game exposes one; document what was and was not covered.
- [ ] For at least one selected game that produces audio, an automated test verifies non-silent game-generated audio samples; interactive browser playback is wired and documented. Do not present a silent emulator as complete.
- [ ] CPU/SPC700 and at least one PPU/DMA timing fixture from the licensed ROM suites pass with reproducible logs/results. Unresolved deviations in additional suites are documented, not concealed.
- [ ] CI performs at least one real-browser smoke/E2E run with a license-cleared ROM; headless regression tests are deterministic and have explicit timeouts.
- [ ] Keyboard and gamepad controls, play/pause/reset, client-side ROM loading, video scaling and audio-start behavior work in a current desktop browser; automated checks cover feasible interactions.
- [ ] No third-party emulation code or unaudited ROMs/assets are included. License/provenance notices and the README state that commercial ROMs are **not shipped** and must be obtained lawfully by users.
- [ ] Document known gaps (e.g. enhancement chips, unsupported mappers, cycle-specific effects, PAL support) and tested game compatibility accurately, without claiming broad commercial compatibility from these homebrew tests.

## Optional validation

- Longer interactive play sessions and cross-browser/gamepad checks.
- Additional cleared games, audio comparisons, screenshot golden baselines, further PPU modes and HiROM; optional commercial-ROM tests using **user-provided** ROMs only.
- Enhancement chips (Super FX/SA-1/etc.), PAL and save states are **not** required for closing this first playable baseline Issue unless a selected mandatory target needs a feature.

## Required post-merge verification

None. Any future live deployment/publishing can be a separate task; do not make a post-merge website deployment a pre-merge condition.
